- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon (especially 1–7 days ahead) and overestimates in late horizon (15–30 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 75+), then fails to correct downward — model lags in recognizing mean reversion.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted: model holds high forecasts too long after peaks, ignoring downward momentum.
- Forecast bias is often downward in low-price regimes (e.g., 60–65 range) and upward in high-price regimes (e.g., 70–75).
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — fails to anticipate price corrections after 3–5 consecutive high values.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are often too low, especially when recent history shows volatility or downward trend.
- Model reacts too slowly to sudden drops — underestimates magnitude and duration of price corrections.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5%, model tends to overcorrect in next period — creates artificial “overshoot” bias.
